Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Reno NV
146 AM PST Tue Nov 24 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* Patchy freezing fog in some eastern CA valleys diminishes by
  later this morning, then winds increase mainly for ridge tops 
  this afternoon through early Wednesday morning.

* Dry conditions are now expected for the peak travel period prior
  to Thanksgiving, except for a few light rain and snow showers in 
  northeast CA late tonight into early Wednesday morning.
 
* Dry and mild weather is favored for much of the Thanksgiving
  holiday weekend, but a more active storm pattern may return from 
  the late weekend into early December. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...

A Pacific storm approaching the west coast today will bring
increased 700 mb S-SW flow of 30-40 kt, leading to increased 
ridge top gusts of 50-70 mph from late this morning through early 
Wednesday morning. However, the moisture and forcing from this 
storm largely falls apart as it reaches the Sierra tonight into 
early Wednesday, with the latest guidance even drier in the 
Sierra from I-80 southward -- chances for any measurable rain or 
snow drop to below 10%. Farther north across northeast CA and far
northwest NV, the shower chances are also slim, with 20% or less 
chance of rainfall amounting to anything more than a trace. The 
remnants of this storm exit to the east during the day Wednesday 
with dry conditions prevailing, so conditions for the peak holiday
travel period leading into Thanksgiving will at least be free 
from weather-related impacts.

For Thanksgiving day through Saturday, building high pressure will 
bring warmer temperatures with highs climbing into the 50s in most
areas. Valley inversions will result in similar daytime highs 
across lower elevations and Sierra communities, with some sites 
above inversion layers having a shot of pushing above 60 degrees. 
By Saturday afternoon, winds ahead of an approaching Pacific storm
could allow more valley sites to reach or exceed 60 degrees. 
These three days should remain dry, although a few scenarios in 
the ensemble guidance indicate a low-end (up to 20%) chance for 
light rain showers near the Oregon border around Friday night. 

While the majority of the holiday weekend looks favorable for
travel across the Sierra, the next storm could bring winter 
conditions for the main passes as soon as Sunday. The timing is 
still in question for this first storm, which appears to be 
trending weaker with a slightly later onset by Sunday night or 
Monday, but holiday travelers should still have winter travel gear
handy in case the storm track/timing shifts again. Then the 
overall trend currently favors a stronger storm by the start of 
December with a more active storm pattern going through the first 
week of the new month. 

MJD

&&

.AVIATION...

KRNO Forecast: VFR conditions with widespread mid-high level cloud
cover and light surface winds prevail into early Wednesday AM. 
Increasing S-SW FL100 winds with gusts 40-50 kt brings periods of
LLWS after 03Z this evening, along with increased turbulence.

Regional Outlook: For KTRK, FZFG with periods of LIFR conditions
continue this morning, while at KTVL patchy shallow FZFG brings 
brief MVFR/IFR conditions, improving at both sites after 15Z. 
Otherwise, VFR conditions and light surface winds prevail through 
early Wednesday AM. Increasing S-SW FL100 winds with gusts 40-50 
kt bring periods of LLWS after 18Z today for KTRK/KTVL and after 
01-03Z this evening at KCXP/KMEV, along with increased turbulence.

24-72 Hour Outlook: Lingering LLWS near the main terminals
(excluding KMMH) diminishes by late Wednesday AM. Otherwise, VFR
conditions with light winds continue through early Friday AM, 
except for high FZFG potential (>80%) with LIFR conditions at 
KTRK Thursday and Friday mornings. Valley inversions may also
lead to increased haze buildup mainly around KRNO Thursday and
Friday mornings, with minor reductions in slantwise visibility.
